1.why: All six screens use a clean, static layout with no visible moving images or pop-ups.

2.why: Large headings, bordered content cards, highlighted notices, and blue action buttons make important items stand out.

3.why: Each screen centers the current task and presents a prominent primary action, although the activity log adds some visual distraction.

4.why: Instructions remain visible on each screen, but the user must complete six stages involving two codes, multiple password rules, and privacy acceptance.

5.why: No password-manager option, autofill control, or remember-me option is visible in any screenshot.

6.why: The interface uses familiar fields, checkboxes, and buttons, but it does not display saved accounts or other recognizable saved items.

7.why: Most text is concise, plainly worded, and displayed at a readable size, though the activity log contains dense technical content.

8.why: No error messages are shown, so there is no observed message that explains a problem and how to fix it.

9.why: The screens provide instructions and password requirements but do not show concrete examples of valid input.

10.why: Password and code actions are clearly labeled when presented, although no face-login choice is offered.

11.why: Each screen presents only one primary task and very few simultaneous choices.

12.why: Screen transitions and the final acceptance message communicate outcomes clearly, although not every intermediate action has an explicit confirmation message.

13.why: Short instructions and safety tips accompany recovery, password creation, code verification, and privacy acceptance.

14.why: A Back button appears only during recovery-code verification, and no explicit retry option or mistake-recovery guidance is shown elsewhere.

15.why: All six screens consistently use the same header, card layout, typography, colors, input styling, and button design.
